title: Is It a Call to Ministry or Just Ambition?
subtitle: Every man who wants a pulpit must learn the difference between being sent and being hungry, because that difference decides everything that comes after.
group: The Inner Life of the Leader

sections.title: Two Fires That Look the Same
sections.body:
There is a fire that God lights. There is a fire a man lights for himself. From the outside they throw the same light, and from the inside, for a long time, they feel identical.

I was twenty-six when I first stood behind a pulpit and felt the room go quiet under my voice, and I told myself it was the Spirit. Some of it was. Some of it was the simple animal pleasure of being listened to by people who had spent their week being ignored. I did not have the honesty then to tell those two things apart. I am not sure I have it fully now.

The call and the ambition both make you want the work. They both get you up early. They both survive discouragement. This is why the search committee cannot tell them apart, and why your own heart cannot be trusted to tell you which one you are running on. The man hungry for significance preaches well. He visits the sick. He raises money. He builds something. For years nothing exposes him, because the fruit of ambition and the fruit of calling look the same on a Sunday morning.

Not a difference you can see. A difference that shows up under pressure.

sections.title: What Each One Does When It Is Denied
sections.body:
Here is the one test I trust, and it is not a feeling. It is a behavior under loss.

Give each fire what it does not want and watch. Calling, when it is overlooked, keeps working. Ambition, when it is overlooked, sulks, campaigns, or leaves. Give a called man a small church that will never grow and he tends it for thirty years and dies happy. Give an ambitious man that same church and within three years he is updating his resume and calling it discernment about a new season.

Watch the man who did not get the position he wanted. Watch whether he can pray honestly for the man who got it. Watch the associate passed over for the senior role, the church planter whose plant failed, the preacher whose better friend got the bigger platform. The call does not require the platform. The ambition cannot live without it.

I have failed this test in private. A friend got an invitation I wanted, and I felt the cold thing move in my chest, and I had to repent of it before I could send the text that said congratulations. That cold thing is the ambition. It is in me still. The work is not to kill it once. The work is to catch it every time it moves.

sections.title: The Call Will Cost You Something Ambition Refuses to Pay
sections.body:
Ambition is a careful accountant. It spends only what it expects to earn back. It will work hard, but it keeps the receipts, and it grows resentful when the return is late.

The call spends what it will not get back. It sits with the dying man who has no money to give and no influence to offer and is unconscious anyway and will not remember you came. It returns the phone call from the family that has criticized you for a decade. It keeps the appointment with the one angry member when the calendar is already full, not because it will help your standing but because the man is a sheep and you are a shepherd and that is what the word means.

Moses did not want the job. Jeremiah begged to be released from it and could not stop. Jonah ran. Paul said woe is me if I do not preach. None of these men sound like a person chasing a platform. They sound like men who have been seized by something they would have gladly put down.

The surest sign of a call is not that you want it. It is that you have tried to lay it down and could not.

sections.title: How to Keep the Two Apart in a Real Week
sections.body:
This is a practical article, so here is the practice. It is not abstract. It happens on a Tuesday.

First, name your wins out loud to one person who is not impressed by you. Your spouse. An old friend. A man who knew you before the title. Ambition cannot stand being un-impressed. The simple act of telling someone the good thing that happened, to someone who only says good, and who does not flatter, starves the hunger of its oxygen.

Second, give away the thing you most want credit for. Hand the best part of the project to someone else and let them be thanked for it. Do it on purpose. Do it when it costs you. The first three times it will feel like dying. That is the right feeling. That is the ambition dying, a little, on schedule.

Third, keep a record of what you do that no one will ever see. Not to admire it. To notice whether you can sustain a ministry that gets no applause, because most of the real work gets none. The hospital at two in the morning. The prayer no congregation hears. If the hidden work has dried up while the visible work flourishes, you already have your answer about which fire you are burning.

Fourth, watch your reaction to other men's success. It is the cleanest mirror you own.

sections.title: Most of Us Are Burning Both Fires
sections.body:
I want to end without resolving it, because the honest answer does not resolve.

Most of us are not running on the call or the ambition. We are running on both, mixed, in proportions we cannot measure and that shift from year to year. The man who tells you his motives are pure is the man you should worry about, because he has stopped looking. The danger is not that you have ambition. The danger is that you have decided you do not.

God has used deeply mixed men. He used me on days when I wanted the room more than I wanted their souls, and he was kind enough not to wait for my motives to be clean before he fed his people through my unclean hands. That is grace, and it is also no excuse, because the same grace that uses you is at work to purify you, and a man who hides from the purifying is refusing half the gift.

So do not wait to be certain you are called. Certainty is not coming. Examine yourself, repent where the cold thing moves, do the hidden work, and keep going. The fire will be tested soon enough.

The pulpit tests it every week. So does the loss you have not yet had.
